another, and stay level. Every entry below is the finding's stable key — the arm
plus the case label — and the gate matches on that key, never on the full
sentence, because the sentence carries record counts and store names that
legitimately move between runs while the DEFECT does not.
CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. An unledgered finding exits 3 (RATCHET EXCEEDED). A

THIS FILE IS SHRINK-ONLY. Adding an entry is not a way to make the gate green;
it is a way to record that a defect was measured before the instrument existed
(BIM30-READINESS-GATES §2.4). Raising the level is forbidden outright (R7: a
measurement raised becomes a permission).
─── THE 6 ENTRIES BELOW ARE THE FIRST HONEST READING, 2026-08-12 ───────────
All six PREDATE this gate. Nothing got worse on the day it landed — the
instrument arrived. Every one lives in code owned by another lane, and this
gate's territory is tools/ only: a gate MEASURES, and when it finds defects it
REPORTS them. See `territory` on each entry for the routing.
S3 (2 entries) is the duplicate-store hazard BIM30-READINESS-GATES §3.2 names as
this gate's core subject, caught in its exact predicted shape: two live
singletons answering for one kind, DISAGREEING after real command seeding.
S1 + S4-VOICE (4 entries) are one mechanism seen from two ends: a bridge that
swallows its command's refusal and resolves the bus promise as success. The
refusal EXISTS and NAMES ITS RULE — it is emitted on a CustomEvent — it simply
never reaches the dispatch site. Success and refusal are the same observable to
the caller, which is the §CONTEXT-DATA-HONESTY failure this repo keeps paying
for: two very different facts printing the same value.

S3 door.measured: @pryzm/geometry-door.doorStore (1 record after seeding) and @pryzm/core-app-model.doorStore are DISTINCT INSTANCES holding 1 and 0 records respectively.
S3 door.why: Two live stores answer for the `door` kind. ProjectSerializer and CommandManager import the geometry-door singleton; anything reaching for the core-app-model one sees an empty model and cannot tell that from 'this project has no doors'.
S3 door.exitCondition: one of the two is deleted or re-exported as the other, so `===` holds and the kind names ONE owner.

S3 window.measured: @pryzm/geometry-window.windowStore (1 record) and @pryzm/core-app-model.windowStore (0 records) are DISTINCT INSTANCES.

S1 slab.updateSystemTypeBatch.measured: Dispatch resolves ok=true and moves ZERO authoritative paths. The handler emits pryzm-slab-type-batch-report with success=false and the reason 'The slab type catalogue is not available here.'
S1 slab.updateSystemTypeBatch.why: The command refuses correctly and names its rule; the plugin bridge discards that result and returns an empty HandlerResult, so the bus reports success. The verb is a no-op that claims to have worked.
S1 slab.updateSystemTypeBatch.territory: plugins/slab/src/handlers/UpdateSlabsSystemTypeBatch.ts, and whatever owns slab/floor system-type catalogue availability — NOT tools/.
S1 slab.updateSystemTypeBatch.exitCondition: either the catalogue is reachable in a composed runtime (the verb then mutates and this entry is struck), or the bridge propagates the refusal so the dispatch does not resolve as success.
